blocks.text: The following Zscaler-issued signing certificates can be used to enroll Zscaler Client Connector and App Connectors:

blocks.item: Root: The root (i.e., parent) certificate for the Client and Connector signing certificates.

Client: A Private Access (ZPA) signing certificate that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connector. The certificate's trust is established by the Zscaler public key infrastructure (PKI). Its parent certificate is the Zscaler Root certificate. Private Access automatically uses this to sign certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connector, unless you configure another Zscaler-issued certificate.
Connector: A signing certificate for Private Access that can be used for enrollment certificates issued to Zscaler Client Connectors. The certificate's trust is also established by the Zscaler PKI.

blocks.text: These signing certificates are 2048-bit key RSA certificates, which support TLS 1.2 connections (with cipher suite ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256).

The certificate used to enroll a Private Service Edge must have the same root certificate used by the enrollment certificate for enrolling App Connectors and Zscaler Client Connector. To learn more, see About Enrollment Certificates, Configuring Private Service Edges, and Generating Zscaler-Issued Enrollment Certificates.
